answer: Stamp every identity's verified work with a unique pigment derived from its hardware-bound key — a color fingerprint that cannot be copied or transferred. A lone sparrow earns its own pigment only through real peer-audited tasks, so in the tundra of fresh registrations an unpigmented identity starts with zero weight. When many identities share near-identical pigment lineages, the network discounts their votes as one actor, forcing a sybil farmer to pay full work cost to dye each clone.
